invalid_if: The document is silent on whether it binds
A provision listed as non-binding is drafted as an obligation elsewhere in the document
The recitals or the opening describe the document as a binding agreement
name: Status of this Term Sheet
title: Status of this Term Sheet
text:
This Term Sheet records the terms on which the Investor proposes to make the Investment in the Company. Its legal effect is as follows.
(a) The following provisions are legally binding on the Parties from the date of this Term Sheet (the "Binding Provisions"): this provision; the provisions headed "Exclusivity", "Confidentiality and Costs" and "Expiry"; and the provisions on governing law, jurisdiction and dispute resolution.
(b) Every other provision of this Term Sheet states the terms the Parties presently propose. It is not legally binding. It creates no obligation on any Party to make or accept the Investment, to issue or subscribe for any security, or to enter into the Definitive Agreements, and no Party has any claim against another if the Investment does not proceed, except under a Binding Provision.
(c) Where a non-binding provision describes something a Party is to do or not to do, it describes what the Parties propose the Definitive Agreements will provide, and imposes no obligation now.
(d) "Definitive Agreements" means the share subscription agreement, the shareholders' agreement and the amendments to the Articles of Association of the Company by which the Investment is to be documented, in the form the Parties may agree. The Investment becomes binding only when, and to the extent that, the Definitive Agreements are executed.
(e) Nothing in this Term Sheet creates a partnership, a joint venture or an agency between any of the Parties.

legal_basis.note: An agreement is a contract only if the parties intend to create legal relations
Agreements whose meaning is not certain are void; a term sheet leaving the essential terms to later agreement is not itself the investment contract

authoring_note: The most important provision in a term sheet. Whether a term sheet binds is decided on the document as a whole, so the binding provisions are listed by heading and every other provision is drafted as a proposal. Sub-clause (c) is a backstop, not a licence: the coherence checks still fail any non-binding provision drafted as an obligation.
d4_44: Rebuilt 9 Oct 2026. Non-binding provisions are drafted as proposals ('it is proposed that ... be'), never as obligations, so the wording agrees with the Status provision.
